title: Orrery — an orbital playground
description: An original, self-contained Three.js solar-system toy with a cinematic star field, locally generated planet textures, a luminous Sun, eight orbiting planets, Saturn's rings, and Earth's Moon. Includes direct scene selection, accessible planet buttons, a reference-fact inspector, smooth planet-follow camera, orbit and zoom controls, pause/resume, speed adjustment, reset, orbit-path and name toggles, responsive layouts, reduced-motion support, and a clearly labelled WebGL fallback.

tests.outcome: Passed with exit code 0, both before and after the repair. Final Vite 7.3.6 build transformed 7 modules in 2.42 seconds and produced in-memory assets/index-C1O1KBvL.js, assets/index-C7k6LXXv.css, and index.html. No build output was written.

repairsMade: Changed playback SVG icon visibility to toggle the hidden attribute explicitly, avoiding reliance on an HTML-only hidden property. Reran both prescribed checks successfully.
knownLimitations: Browser localhost access was unavailable; no browser, WebGL runtime, visual, or device checks were performed or claimed.
Planet sizes, orbital distances, inclination, surface artwork, and motion are deliberately stylized. Reference facts are rounded and clearly distinguished from the toy's geometry.

If WebGL initialization fails or its context is lost, the scene controls are disabled and the labelled fallback remains readable. Planet selection and reference information remain usable. Context restoration requires reloading.
